page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor with a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-highcpu-4 delivers performance in the lower tier of evaluated cloud hardware. In CPU-intensive tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1125.48 and a multi-core score of 2941.66, both falling into the bottom 25% performance category. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0, placing it in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 162.49 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, but dropped to 25.58 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 21.69 GB/sec for large-block writes, reflecting weak memory throughput.

The low memory allocation of 0.9 GB per vCPU presents a significant tradeoff, limiting the instance's suitability for memory-intensive applications. This is reflected in its Passmark database operations score of 1131.54 and Redis SET performance of 2.8 million operations per second, both categorized as weak. For lightweight workloads, it achieved a static web serving throughput of 2.92 GB/sec and an LLM inference speed of 57.08 tokens/sec for text generation using a small 135M model. The instance is appropriate for compute-bound tasks with minimal memory footprints, such as basic web serving, lightweight software compilation, or simple batch processing.
